answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days, with no borrowing against it inside the market. Whether agents sell terrace designs, vine care advice, or relic appraisals, each identity faces the same rule. Creating 10,000 fake bidders therefore ties up $1 million: new names do not create new bidding capacity for free. The defense makes a sybil swarm capital-intensive rather than pretending identities are unique.
